headline: Five of seven majors sit above their 200-day line, but the last week has been a slow leak, not a rally
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's mostly intact. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses in place, which is the kind of alignment that says the longer trend is still up. Doge and Cardano are the odd ones out, both below their 200-day lines with no golden cross, and both are also the deepest below their 12-month highs (-71.1% and -77.8% respectively) alongside XRP at -56.8% and Solana at -59.4%. So the broad trend structure favors the majors, but the drawdowns from highs tell you this recovery has a long way to go before anyone calls it healed.

Layer on momentum and you find a quiet disagreement. RSI readings across the board sit in the mid-50s (Bitcoin 54.4, Ethereum 59.5, Solana 54.8, BNB 55.5), which is neutral-to-firm, not overbought, not broken. But every single asset's MACD sits below its signal line. That's a trend that's resting or cooling, not accelerating, even while the 200-day structure stays bullish. Zoom out on bitcoin specifically: down 0.2% on the day, down 5.1% over the week, up 22.8% over the month. Three different stories depending on which window you read, and the honest one is that the monthly advance has stalled into a weekly pullback without breaking the longer trend.

Positioning adds some texture. Bitcoin funding on OKX sits at 0.0053% per 8 hours (5.8% annualized), which is modestly positive, longs paying shorts to hold the bet, but nowhere near the frothy extremes that precede violent unwinds. The long/short account ratio of 1.71 says more accounts are positioned long than short. Liquidations in the last 2 hours skewed hard against shorts ($527,940 wiped out versus $12,337 on longs), consistent with the market grinding sideways-to-up and squeezing the people who bet against it. Doge stands out with 11% annualized funding and a 4.53 long/short ratio, an expensive, crowded long by comparison, though open interest there ($89.2M) is small next to bitcoin's $2.18B.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. Whale wallets moved a net $226,996,468 onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, with the biggest single moves including $164.9M in BTC to Coinbase and stablecoin transfers to Kraken and Binance. Widen to the weekly view and the pattern isn't new: of the last four weeks, three showed net movement onto exchanges (Aug 23: $1,062M, Aug 30: $659M, and the current week ending Sep 13: $827M), interrupted by one week of outflows (Sep 06: $494M off exchanges). Coins moving toward exchanges is usually read as potential sell-side supply positioning, not confirmed selling, but the direction has now shown up in three of four recent weeks. Meanwhile the ETF tape splits by asset: bitcoin ETFs logged a $13.2M outflow on 11 Sep, part of a four-day same-direction streak totaling a $288.1M net outflow over five sessions, while ether ETFs took in $216.4M that same day, essentially the whole five-session net of $222.8M in one print. Traditional finance is leaning out of bitcoin and into ether at the same time whales are shuffling coin onto exchanges. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, grew a modest 1.35% over 30 days to $310.2B, not a surge of fresh cash waiting to deploy.

Sentiment reads 61, labeled Greed, sitting mid-range against its own 30-day band of 31 to 74. That's crowd mood leaning cheerful while the tape underneath shows five straight days of bitcoin ETF outflows, a fourth consecutive week (out of four) tilted toward exchange inflows, and MACD cooling across every major. The gap between how people feel and what the money is actually doing is the story today, not any single number.

Worth watching from here: whether bitcoin ETF flows flip back to net inflow and break the current four-day outflow streak, whether the weekly whale flow turns from onto-exchanges to off-exchanges the way it briefly did in the week ending Sep 06, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on bitcoin or ether, which would mark the cooling trend re-accelerating rather than just resting.
